ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: This account is overwhelmingly rank-constrained, not budget-constrained. Across the key non-brand search campaigns you’re only capturing 5–7% search impression share while losing 93–95% to rank, despite budget utilization sitting ~56–59% and lost IS to budget at 0%. Auction pressure is extreme (competitors top-of-page 73.2% vs your 15.2%; your outranking share 9.1%), and you also have pockets of waste/intent mismatch (e.g., “insurance company phone number” QS 3.0 at €2,605.80 with €1,371.47 cost/conv) that drag effective rank and efficiency.
notable_patterns: Non-brand demand is largely untapped due to rank, not budget: Auto/Home/Life search IS is 6%/5%/7% with lost rank 94%/95%/93% and lost budget 0% in all three, while budget utilization is only 57.2%/58.5%/56.2%.

Even high-quality keywords aren’t getting served, pointing to insufficient Ad Rank via bids/auction pressure rather than relevance alone: “auto insurance germany” QS 9.0 has only 5.0% IS (95% lost to rank); “home insurance cost” QS 8.5 has 5.5% IS (94.5% lost to rank).

Competitors consistently win premium placement: average top-of-page rate is 15.2% for you vs 73.2% for competitors; Nordkreuz Assurance is above you 96.5% of the time and at top-of-page 82.6% vs your 17.1%.

A large slice of impressions is coming from competitor-brand queries that don’t engage: 35,700 competitor-brand zero-click impressions, and 48.3% of search-term impressions are from zero-click competitor terms (e.g., “bluewave insurance”, “harborline mutual”, “crestfield direct”).

campaign_findings.diagnosis: You’re only capturing 6% search impression share while losing 94% to rank, with 0% lost to budget and only 57.2% budget utilization—this is an Ad Rank/position problem, not spend caps. Efficiency is also weak (ROAS 0.7) suggesting current coverage is skewing to poorer-intent queries while you miss stronger ones.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Restructure around high-intent quote/comparison terms and raise competitiveness (bids/targets) on the proven high-QS terms (e.g., “car insurance quote”, “auto insurance germany”) while cutting/negating low-intent leakage; aim to materially lift top-of-page rate and impression share before scaling budget.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: The campaign is effectively not participating in the auction (5% IS; 95% lost to rank) despite 0% lost to budget and 58.5% budget utilization. Average quality score is low (4.1), which will further suppress Ad Rank and keep CPC inefficient at any meaningful coverage.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Rebuild keyword-to-ad-to-landing alignment to lift QS (starting with ad groups around “home insurance cost”) and only then increase competitiveness on the best-intent segments; remove/negate process/claims informational traffic that’s absorbing spend without proportional returns.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Rank is the binding constraint (7% IS; 93% lost to rank; 0% lost to budget; 56.2% budget utilization), compounded by an extremely low average quality score (2.0) that makes it very hard to win auctions. Current ROAS is 0.89, consistent with paying for low-intent educational queries while missing comparison/quote demand.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Split informational vs. commercial intent, pause/negate the worst educational terms (e.g., “what is life insurance” QS 4.5 with €613.56 cost/conv), and rebuild RSAs/landing pages for “life insurance comparison” intent to raise QS and regain impression share.

recommendation_cards.title: Win back non-brand impression share by fixing Ad Rank (bids + structure) on the highest-intent terms
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Your three in-scope non-brand campaigns are barely serving (Auto 6% IS / 94% lost to rank; Home 5% / 95%; Life 7% / 93%) with 0% lost to budget and only ~56–59% budget utilization—so demand isn’t being capped by budgets. Even strong-QS terms aren’t showing: “auto insurance germany” QS 9.0 has 5% IS with 95% lost to rank; “car insurance quote” QS 8.0 has 6% IS with 94% lost to rank.
recommended_steps: Create separate ad groups (or standalone campaigns if needed) for the high-intent quote/comparison keywords listed (e.g., “auto insurance germany”, “car insurance quote”, “home insurance cost”, “life insurance comparison”) and isolate them from broader/mixed-intent terms.

Increase competitiveness specifically on these segments (raise bids / relax efficiency targets) until top-of-page rate materially improves; keep changes scoped so you can measure lift without inflating low-intent traffic.
Add tighter match types and query controls for these segments so incremental rank is spent on commercial intent rather than informational queries.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Top-of-page rate moving from 15.2% toward 25–30%+ and search impression share in non-brand campaigns rising from ~5–7% into the teens without ROAS deteriorating further.

recommendation_cards.title: Cut low-intent spend that is inflating costs and dragging effective rank
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Several queries/keywords show extremely poor economics: “insurance company phone number” (QS 3.0) spent €2,605.80 at €1,371.47 per conversion; “home insurance claims process” (QS 4.0) spent €2,248.95 at €244.45 per conversion; “what is life insurance” spent €858.99 at €613.56 per conversion. This spend is competing with your quote/comparison terms for auction pressure while your non-brand IS remains ~5–7%.
recommended_steps: Add/expand intent negatives (e.g., phone number, customer service, claims, process, what is, definition) in the non-brand campaigns, then re-check search terms after 48–72 hours for variants.
Move any genuinely necessary informational coverage into a separate, tightly capped campaign so it can’t suppress the main quote/comparison coverage.
Reallocate freed spend headroom into the isolated high-intent ad groups where rank is the limiting factor.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Cost/conv on non-brand dropping materially (start by eliminating the €244–€1,371 cost/conv pockets) while impression share on the high-intent ad groups increases.

recommendation_cards.title: Stop competitor-brand “zero-click” leakage and refocus coverage on terms that can convert
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Competitor-brand queries are a major volume driver but low engagement: 35,700 competitor-brand zero-click impressions, and 48.3% of search-term impressions come from zero-click competitor terms (e.g., “bluewave insurance”, “harborline mutual”, “crestfield direct”). Only one competitor-brand term is shown converting (“nordkreuz insurance quote”: 1.0 conversion).
recommended_steps: Add competitor brand negatives for the identified zero-click terms (Bluewave/Harborline/Crestfield) at the appropriate level to prevent repeat exposure.
Keep (or test separately) the one competitor term that has evidence of conversion (“nordkreuz insurance quote”) in a small, controlled ad group with bespoke ad copy.
After exclusions, review impression mix to ensure reclaimed inventory shifts toward “quote/comparison/cost” intent rather than other low-intent categories.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Share of impressions from competitor-brand zero-click terms falling from 48.3% to <20% while overall non-brand conversions hold or improve.

recommendation_cards.title: Fix the life & home Quality Score bottleneck to make rank gains affordable
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: The Home and Life campaigns have weak average quality scores (Home QS 4.1; Life QS 2.0) alongside extreme lost rank (95% and 93%). This combination usually forces you to overpay for position or (as seen here) fail to enter auctions consistently.
recommended_steps: Rebuild RSAs and landing page alignment per intent theme (e.g., separate “comparison”, “cost”, “quote” from educational intent); ensure the keyword appears in headlines and on-page above the fold for those themes.
Tighten ad group keyword lists to improve predicted CTR and relevance (fewer, more homogeneous keywords per group).
After QS lifts, revisit bids/targets to buy back impression share with less CPC inflation.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Average QS in Life rising from ~2 toward 4+ and Home from ~4.1 toward 6+, accompanied by reduced lost-to-rank percentage in those campaigns.

already_working: Budgets are not currently constraining delivery: impression share lost to budget is 0% across every campaign listed, and budget utilization is only ~51–59% (e.g., Auto 57.2%, Home 58.5%, Life 56.2%).
Brand coverage is relatively strong: Brand Search - DE has 85% search impression share with only 15% lost to rank and a healthy ROAS of 4.7.

Ad asset quality is not the main limiter: 80% of ads are rated Good or Excellent (3 Excellent, 1 Good), so the biggest gains are more about auction competitiveness and query mix than rewriting everything.

email_copy.subject: EUR 188,014 sitting behind a rank bottleneck (9.02% IS, 0.0% lost to budget)

With a daily budget of EUR 52,768, you still have room to capture materially more non-brand demand if we fix position and query mix.

Your non-brand coverage is well below where the market is trending: you’re at 9.02% impression share versus a 21.0% vertical average, and you’re losing 91.0% to rank (not budget).
The highest-intent themes you want are growing: “home insurance cost” is up 19% and “cheap auto insurance” up 33% — the exact moments where being rank-constrained is most expensive.
email_copy.stat_sub: Unlocked by improving Ad Rank and cleaning up intent — not by raising caps.
email_copy.impact_line: Right now the account is overwhelmingly rank-constrained: only 9.02% impression share with 0.0% lost to budget, but 91.0% lost to rank. That gap translates to EUR 188,014 in incremental revenue opportunity this quarter if we win back premium placement on quote/comparison intent and stop spending impressions on terms that don’t convert.
email_copy.scope_intro: Below is a quick breakdown of where that upside is sitting across your core non-brand campaigns, so you can see where rank and intent fixes will pay back fastest.
email_copy.cards_intro: Here are the specific, high-leverage changes that will move the needle first — the goal is to buy back visibility on proven commercial intent while preventing low-intent traffic from dragging down effective rank.
email_copy.working_intro: A few things are already in a good place — which is why this is more of a “reposition and refocus” job than a rebuild from scratch.
email_copy.opportunity_intro: If we execute the fixes below, the payoff is straightforward: moving from today’s 9.02% toward a 21.0% share adds meaningful scale (impressions and clicks) while keeping the plan grounded in your current click rate assumptions — and it ladders directly into the EUR 188,014 upside.
